units.title: Argument and Explanation: Claims, Evidence, Counterclaims and Structure
skills: Introduce a claim and organize reasons and evidence clearly
Acknowledge an opposing claim and respond to it
Organize information by comparison, contrast, or cause and effect
Use transitions, a formal style and a strong conclusion
vocab: claim
the position a writer argues for in an argument
counterclaim
an opposing view that disagrees with the writer’s claim
rebuttal
the writer’s answer that shows why the counterclaim is weaker
credible source
a source that is trustworthy because experts wrote or checked it
compare-and-contrast structure
a way of organizing that shows how two things are alike and different
formal style
serious, clear language without slang, used for school and work writing

passage.title: Plastic Bottles Should Go
passage.intro: Yousef is writing an argument essay for the school newspaper. Read his draft and answer the questions.
paras: (1) Every day, students at our school throw away hundreds of plastic water bottles. (2) The school should stop selling single-use plastic bottles in the cafeteria. (3) Most of these bottles are never recycled. (4) Instead, they end up in landfills or in the ocean, where they can take hundreds of years to break down. (5) Some students say that bottled water is more convenient. (6) The cafeteria also sells sandwiches and fruit. (7) Refill stations would make it just as easy to get clean water, and reusable bottles would save families money.

items.stem: Which sentence states Yousef’s claim?
options: sentence 1
sentence 2
sentence 3
sentence 5
items.skill: States a clear claim or thesis

items.stem: Which sentence does NOT support the claim and should be removed?
options: sentence 3
sentence 4
sentence 6
sentence 7
items.skill: Identifies a sentence that does not belong

items.stem: Which transition would BEST begin sentence 7 to respond to the opposing view in sentence 5?
options: Similarly,
As a result,
For example,
However,
items.skill: Acknowledges and answers an opposing claim

items.stem: Which piece of evidence would BEST support sentence 3?
options: A national study found that fewer than one in three plastic bottles is recycled.
Many students prefer cold water to warm water after a long recess outside.
Plastic bottles come in many sizes, colors and shapes in most large stores today.
Our cafeteria is open from eight o’clock in the morning until two o’clock.
items.skill: Chooses relevant evidence to support a point

items.stem: Which source would be the MOST credible for evidence about plastic in the ocean?
options: a comment posted under a video about plastic art
a report from a university marine science department
a blog post by a student who visited the beach once
an advertisement for a company that sells reusable bottles
items.skill: Chooses a useful source or research question

items.stem: Which sentence would be the BEST conclusion for the essay?
options: Many students drink a lot of water during the day, especially after sports and physical education classes.
Some people think that plastic bottles are useful, and some other people think that they are not.
By replacing plastic bottles with refill stations, our school can protect the environment and save money.
Plastic was invented more than one hundred years ago by scientists who worked in laboratories.
items.skill: Chooses an effective concluding sentence

passage.intro: Reem is writing an informative report that compares two kinds of camels. Read her draft and answer the questions.

passage.title: The Power Outage
passage.intro: Bader is writing a story about a night when the power went out. Read his draft and answer the questions.
paras: (1) The lights flickered twice and then went out. (2) The whole apartment was dark. (3) My little sister grabbed my arm. (4) “I can’t see anything,” she said. (5) I felt my way to the kitchen drawer and found a flashlight. (6) We sat by the window and watched the dark city. (7) Then, one by one, the stars appeared above the rooftops.

passage.title: Research Notes: The Empty Quarter
passage.intro: Fahad is writing a report about the Rub’ al Khali. Read the source and his draft, then answer the questions.
paras: **Source:** “The Rub’ al Khali, or Empty Quarter, covers about 650,000 square kilometers of the Arabian Peninsula. It is one of the largest sand deserts in the world. Some of its dunes rise more than 250 meters high. Despite the harsh conditions, animals such as the Arabian oryx, sand cats and desert foxes live there.”
**Draft**

(1) The Empty Quarter is a giant desert. (2) It covers about 650,000 square kilometers. (3) Its dunes are really, really big. (4) Even though it is very hot and dry, some animals still survive there. (5) People have crossed the desert by camel for centuries. (6) In 1931, a British explorer named Bertram Thomas became the first known European to cross it.

sentence 3
sentence 5

items.skill: Keeps a consistent formal style and objective tone

options: Its dunes are big, and some are even bigger than others.

Some of its sand dunes are taller than 250 meters.
items.skill: Uses notes and facts accurately in writing

dependent clause
a clause that cannot stand alone, often starting with because, although or when
standard English
the form of English expected in formal writing and speaking

paras: (1) Before paper was invented, people wrote on clay tablets, animal skins and silk. (2) These materials were heavy, expensive or difficult to make. (3) Around the year 105, a Chinese official named Cai Lun improved a way to make paper from tree bark, old rags and plants. (4) For centuries, the Chinese kept their method a secret. (5) In the 700s, papermaking spread to Samarkand and then to Baghdad, where paper mills were built. (6) From there, the knowledge traveled to north africa and Europe. (7) Paper made books more cheaper, and more people could learn to read.

passage.intro: Hassan wrote a story about a chess tournament. Read his draft and answer the questions.
paras: (1) The clock ticked loudly as I stared at the chessboard. (2) My opponent, a tall boy from Dammam, had just captured my queen. (3) My hands was sweating, and my heart pounded. (4) I remembered what my coach always said: “Never give up until the game is over.” (5) I studied the board and noticed that his king was unprotected. (6) Slowly, I moved my knight forward. (7) “Checkmate” I said quietly.

passage.title: Zoos: Helpful or Harmful?
passage.intro: Shatha wrote an argument essay. Read her draft and answer the questions.
paras: (1) Modern zoos play an important role in protecting wildlife. (2) Many zoos run breeding programs for endangered species. (3) The Arabian oryx, for example was saved from extinction partly through breeding programs in zoos. (4) Zoos also teach visitors about animals and their habitats. (5) Critics claim that animals in zoos are unhappy in small cages. (6) However, the best zoos now design large spaces that look like the animals’ natural homes. (7) If we want future generations to see these animals, we must supports good zoos.
